note.explanation: Transition elements are metals found in groups 3 to 12. They have properties such as high strength, high melting and boiling points, variable oxidation states, and coloured compounds. Some transition metals or their compounds act as catalysts in important industrial processes and in automobile exhaust systems.
examples: Iron acts as a catalyst in the Haber process to produce ammonia.
Nickel is used as a catalyst to hydrogenate oils and make solid margarine.
note.simple: Transition elements are metals in the centre of the periodic table. Some help chemical reactions happen faster as catalysts.

note.answer: Transition elements are metals in groups 3 to 12. They often have high strength and high melting and boiling points, show variable oxidation states, and form coloured compounds. Some are used as catalysts.

rationales: This is correct: the section places transition elements in groups 3 to 12 at the centre of the modern periodic table.
This is incorrect: group 1 is not the transition-element region.
This is incorrect: groups 13 to 18 are not the groups named for transition elements in this section.
This is incorrect: transition elements are not limited to period 1.

mcqs.stem: Which property is characteristic of transition elements according to this section?
rationales: This is correct: the section says transition metals show variable oxidation states.
This is incorrect: transition elements are metals, not all gases.
This is incorrect: the section says their compounds are often coloured.
This is incorrect: the section says their melting and boiling points are high.

mcqs.stem: Which transition metal is used as a catalyst in the Haber process?
rationales: This is correct: iron is shown as the catalyst in the Haber process reaction.
This is incorrect: nickel is used to catalyse hydrogenation of oils.
This is incorrect: palladium is listed as a catalytic-converter catalyst.
This is incorrect: platinum is listed as a catalytic-converter catalyst and was originally used in the contact process.

mcqs.stem: Which catalyst is now preferred for the oxidation of sulphur dioxide in the contact process?
rationales: This is correct: vanadium pentoxide, V₂O₅, is now preferred for this step.
This is incorrect: nickel is used to catalyse hydrogenation of oils.
This is incorrect: iron is used in the Haber process.
This is incorrect: rhodium is used in catalytic converters.

mcqs.stem: Which set of catalysts is named for catalytic converters?
rationales: This is correct: the section names platinum, palladium and rhodium.
This is incorrect: the section does not give this as the catalytic-converter set.
This is incorrect: these are not the catalysts named for catalytic converters.
This is incorrect: these are halogens, not the catalysts listed for catalytic converters.

mcqs.stem: What product is made when oils are hydrogenated using nickel as a catalyst?
rationales: This is correct: nickel catalyses hydrogenation of oils to give solid margarine.
This is incorrect: ammonia is made in the Haber process using iron.
This is incorrect: sulphuric acid is made in the contact process.
This is incorrect: sulphur trioxide is an intermediate in the contact process, not the product of oil hydrogenation.

written.text: Why are transition elements different from normal elements?
written.finalAnswer: Transition elements are different because they have variable oxidation states, often form coloured compounds, and can act as catalysts; they are also generally hard metals with high densities and high melting and boiling points.

written.text: Explain the role of catalytic converter in an automobile.
written.finalAnswer: A catalytic converter is a device in an automobile's exhaust that converts more harmful gases produced in the engine into gases that do not pollute the atmosphere. Platinum, palladium and rhodium are used as catalysts in it.

written.text: V₂O₅ catalyst is preferred over platinum in the oxidation of sulphur dioxide. Give reasons.
written.finalAnswer: Platinum is rendered inactive by arsenic impurity in sulphur dioxide, so vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) is now preferred as the catalyst.

rubric.why: The answer must name the catalyst preferred instead.

explain.title: Where transition elements are found
explain.body: Elements present at the centre of the modern periodic table from group 3 to group 12 are called d block elements or transition elements. They are metals.

explain.title: Properties of transition elements
explain.body: Transition elements are often hard and have higher densities. Their melting and boiling points are high. They show variable oxidation states, and the compounds they form are often coloured. They are malleable and ductile.

explain.title: Transition metals as catalysts
explain.body: Transition metals and their compounds function as catalysts in many important chemical reactions. Metals often absorb other substances on their surface and activate them in this process.

explain.title: Catalyst uses in the section
explain.body: Iron is used in the Haber process to make ammonia. Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) is now preferred over platinum for oxidising sulphur dioxide in the contact process. Platinum, palladium and rhodium are used in catalytic converters, and nickel is used to hydrogenate oils to make solid margarine.

mistakes: Do not confuse the catalyst in the Haber process (iron) with the catalyst used for hydrogenating oils (nickel).
Do not say platinum is now preferred in the contact process; the section says V₂O₅ is now preferred because arsenic impurity renders platinum inactive.
When explaining a catalytic converter, do not omit that it is used in an automobile exhaust and changes harmful gases into gases that do not pollute the atmosphere.
Do not describe all transition-element compounds as coloured; the section says they are often coloured.
